records.claimSummary: Options are scored by weighted criteria: operational effort 40%, cost 30%, developer experience 20%, portability 10%.
records.conditionSummary: Two must-haves gate the scoring: an option failing either is out regardless of its score.
records.mustConvey: must-haves; fail either -> out regardless of score
records.bindingReason: A high-scoring option that fails a must-have would wrongly look selectable from the weights alone.
records.notes: g1 takeaway: 'Options must meet mandatory criteria, then are scored by weighted factors.'

records.conditionSummary: Figure assumes current volume; at 3x volume it would be roughly $900/month.
records.mustConvey: assumes current volume; ~$900 at three times volume
records.bindingReason: At the 3x volume the criteria require, $310 is wrong by about 3x.
records.notes: u5_n1's Notes cell 'Priced per million requests; grows with volume' conveys volume dependence (not the $900). Chart u5_n2 has no arrows; g5 takeaway 'current and projected volume' is too vague to count as frame.

records.claimSummary: The self-hosted broker's cost stays flat as volume grows.
records.conditionSummary: Only until the cluster needs a fourth machine.
records.mustConvey: until a fourth machine is needed
records.bindingReason: Once a fourth machine is needed the broker's cost rises, so 'stays flat' is false.
records.notes: intra-sentence. u5_a1 says 'would remain flat' and concludes broker is cheaper at higher volume, without the fourth-machine bound; no arrow to u5_n3.

records.claimSummary: Option A needs almost no operational work.
records.conditionSummary: At-least-once delivery: every job handler must be made idempotent before switching; today only the email handler is.
records.mustConvey: every handler idempotent before switching; only email handler is today
records.bindingReason: Ongoing operational work stays near zero; the condition is an up-front requirement and cost on adopting A.
records.notes: Binding debatable: could be 'claim' if read as 'A is the low-effort option'.

records.claimSummary: With Option A, failed messages move to a dead-letter queue automatically.
records.conditionSummary: Local development's emulator does not support dead-lettering.
records.mustConvey: local emulator does not support dead-lettering
records.bindingReason: Dead-lettering still works in production; the condition limits local testing (a scored criterion).

records.claimSummary: Self-hosted broker needs about 12 hours a month of team effort.
records.conditionSummary: No one on the team has run this broker in production, so 12 hours is an estimate, not a measurement.
records.mustConvey: estimate, not measured / no production experience
records.bindingReason: Read as a measured figure, 'about 12 hours' overstates confidence in the effort that carries 40% weight.
records.notes: u2_n1 itself ('Estimated 12 hours/month (not measured)') states claim and condition together; u2_fs1 is linked to it by arrow. Cost table and chart in g5 have only the frame-level g2->g5 arrow.

records.claimSummary: Option C writes the job in the same transaction, so a job can never be lost between commit and enqueue.
records.conditionSummary: Only for jobs created inside the billing database transaction; reporting-service jobs (own database) don't get it.
records.mustConvey: only jobs created inside the billing DB transaction; not reporting-service jobs
records.bindingReason: For reporting-service jobs, 'a job can never be lost' is false.
records.notes: u2_a1 says 'strong transactional guarantees for billing-related jobs': scope is recognisable but reporting-service exclusion not explicit; medium.

records.claimSummary: Database job table costs $0 extra infrastructure, using spare capacity on the existing primary.
records.conditionSummary: Polling adds read load to the primary database, the main risk at month-end.
records.mustConvey: read load on primary; main risk at month-end
records.bindingReason: $0 extra stays true; the condition is a risk/cost of using the primary.

records.claimSummary: Option C sustained 1,200 jobs/min at 18 ms p95; at 2,000 jobs/min CPU 85% and p95 240 ms.
records.conditionSummary: 1,800 jobs/min not tested and staging is about a quarter of production size, so results may not carry over.
records.mustConvey: 1,800 not tested; staging ~1/4 production size; may not carry over
records.bindingReason: Read as production capacity, the figures could wrongly suggest C meets the 1,800/min must-have.

records.claimSummary: Option A's documented throughput is far above our peak.
records.conditionSummary: That is the provider's figure, not ours; Options A and B were not load-tested.
records.mustConvey: provider's figure, not our own test
records.bindingReason: Stated as our finding, it would wrongly imply A was verified against the 1,800/min must-have.
records.notes: intra-sentence attribution kept because it decides whether the must-have is evidenced.

records.claimSummary: The note does not recommend an option; the decision is deferred.
records.conditionSummary: Deferred until Option C is measured at 1,800 jobs per minute on a production-sized database.
records.mustConvey: 1,800 jobs per minute on a production-sized database
records.bindingReason: Without the specific bar, any further C test (e.g. at lower rate or on staging) would seem to unblock the decision.
records.notes: u3_n1 has 'production-sized database' but not 1,800; u3_n1 -> u3_n6 (shape 'Option C') -> u3_n7 is two hops, not a direct link. g3 takeaway lacks the bar. u0_ax1 ('presents the chosen background job queue') contradicts u41 outright.

records.claimSummary: In the in-process worker pool, a deploy or crash loses jobs.
records.conditionSummary: Only jobs queued but not yet started are lost.
records.bindingReason: 'Deploys lose jobs' overstates the loss to in-progress/finished jobs.

notes: No records for u2/u4/u5 (context facts), u20 itself (it is the must-have, carried by u1_n1), u29/u31 (features/trade-offs without a limiting clause), u45 (Option B open requirement; standalone), u47/u48 (attribution/thanks). Systematic: the cost table and chart in g5 repeat figures whose caveats live only in g2 or within g5 text nodes without arrows. u0_ax1 claims the note 'presents the chosen' queue, contradicting the source's explicit no-recommendation (not a condition record, but a fidelity error).
